newsitem.title: FINLAND: SAK'S PARMANNE WANTS LONG, LOW-INFLATION PAY DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SAK'S PARMANNE WANTS LONG, LOW-INFLATION PAY DEAL.

text.p: Pertti Parmanne, chief economist at the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK), proposes a stability package, including a long-term pay deal aimed to keep inflation low, to support economic growth, SAK said in a statement on Tuesday.

"Parmanne proposes, in order to support economic growth, a broad stability package, among whose elements would be a long-term stabilising pay deal, wage hikes adjusted to low inflation and a tax reform to remove the danger of a bourse bubble," SAK said.
The risk of overheating should be dampened by adjusting corporate taxes and hiking and extending real estate taxes to land and forest property, it said.
Corporate taxation should abandon the current depreciation system which favours tax evation and punishes the use of labour, SAK said.
SAK is Finland's largest labour organisation and represents some 1.1 million mostly blue-collar workers.
